comments.note: DataGrid.php: The preg_match pattern '/^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/' enforces proper kebab-case but intentionally does not allow single-word IDs like 'grid' (no hyphen required). Current behavior — 'my-grid' passes, 'grid' also passes (no hyphen required). This is correct per the requirements.

JsonFileStorage (src/Grids/Storage/Types/JsonFileStorage.php) uses a looser regex '^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9\-_]*$' for grid ID validation, including uppercase letters and underscores, while DataGrid now enforces strict kebab-case. These could diverge silently — e.g. a future caller could bypass DataGrid validation and pass a storage directly. Consider aligning JsonFileStorage's validation regex to the same strict kebab-case pattern, or document the intentional divergence.

DataGridException.php previously used untyped class constants (no explicit type). WP-003 adds ERROR_INVALID_GRID_ID as 'public const int'. The three existing constants (ERROR_NO_PAGINATION_PROVIDER, ERROR_NO_VALUE_COLUMN, ERROR_NO_ROW_MANAGER) remain without explicit int type. For consistency, those three should also be typed — but this is out of scope for WP-003.

comments.note: Edge-case analysis: preg_match() return value is checked with !== 1, which correctly handles both 0 (no match) and false (regex error). The regex is a static literal so false will never occur in practice, but the guard is correct idiomatically.

Edge-case analysis: settings() lazy initialisation is sound — calling settings() multiple times returns the same instance. Verified via GridSettingsTest::testStorageIsIsolatedPerGridID which creates two GridSettings instances with the same storage, confirming isolation by gridID works correctly.

Inherited from Developer note: JsonFileStorage uses a looser regex ('^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9\-_]*$') that accepts uppercase and underscores, while DataGrid enforces strict kebab-case. A caller who bypasses DataGrid and constructs a storage directly could silently store data under a non-kebab key. Consider aligning the two validators or documenting the intentional divergence.
No security concerns: ID validation is purely an input-sanity gate. No user-controlled data reaches file paths or SQL at this layer without further validation in JsonFileStorage.

NON-BLOCKING — Divergent ID validation regexes: DataGrid enforces strict kebab-case /^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$/ while JsonFileStorage uses the permissive /^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9\-_]*$/. Since JsonFileStorage::validateGridID() is always called after the DataGrid constructor has already enforced the strict regex, no invalid ID can reach it in normal usage. However, the JsonFileStorage class can be used independently (bypassing DataGrid), which would allow uppercase/underscore IDs to pass storage validation. Recommend aligning JsonFileStorage regex to the strict kebab-case pattern in a follow-up, or documenting the intentional divergence. (Already flagged as medium-debt by Developer.)

NON-BLOCKING — JsonFileStorage::set() silently ignores write failures: file_put_contents() returns false on failure (e.g. permission error, disk full) but the return value is not checked. For a local/LAN deployment target this is acceptable, but a failed write leaves settings silently un-persisted. Consider wrapping in a check and throwing DataGridException in a future hardening pass.

NON-BLOCKING — GridSettings::getItemsPerPage() coerces non-integer stored values via (int)$value without warning. If JSON is manually edited to an invalid string (e.g. 'invalid'), this returns 0 silently instead of null/default. Harmless in a closed write-path, but worth noting for future robustness.
